models.e: the host's own model root supersedes these WSL weights. Every weight's identity was read from its OWN GGUF header (never its filename) and its public source measured, not assumed -- and the grades are recorded as they are, not rounded up: bonsai-27b-q1_0.gguf (Bonsai-27B, 3,803,452,480 B, sha256 17ef842e47450cae...): NO byte-identical artifact -- public BASE MODEL prism-ml/Ternary-Bonsai-27B-gguf, so the quant is reproducible, not re-downloadable; qwen-moe-2.4b-q4_k_m.gguf (Qwen3-MOE, 964,652,928 B, sha256 518b01713cee4762...): NO byte-identical artifact -- public BASE MODEL EschaLabs/escha-runtime-qwen3moe, so the quant is reproducible, not re-downloadable; amd.Instella-MoE-16B-A3B-Think.f16.gguf.Q2_K.gguf (amd.Instella-MoE, 6,514,704,512 B, sha256 ba208940c2d8c66c...): NO byte-identical artifact -- public BASE MODEL amd/Instella-MoE-16B-A3B-Think, so the quant is reproducible, not re-downloadable. Each base model is public and named above, so nothing here is the only copy in existence; the counterpart path is the platform's own model root, which is what actually serves inference. Load evidence for these weights was harvested earlier (the qwen-moe one was MEASURED to load and run; the instella Q2_K was measured to FAIL to load on mainline b10964). Closing record: swarm_v2_artifacts/harvest_groups_closure_20260926.json (block 174).
